695005: An arbitrary file reading vulnerability was discovered in the Pulse Secure SSL VPN, which allowed remote attackers to read sensitive files on the server. 695041: The activation code used to enable two-factor authentication (2FA) via SMS on Shopify could be reused to log in to an account, allowing an attacker to gain access without the victim's knowledge.

710813: A vulnerability was discovered in Adobe Experience Manager that allowed logging in with default credentials. The vulnerability was discovered by fuzzing and accessing the panel, but it was not being used at the time. The impact was considered medium.

761573: A XSS vulnerability was found on mtnplay.co.zm that allowed for the injection of malicious javascript code through the search form.
765825: Sensitive information, including an API password for Yubikey hardware authentication software, was disclosed in a .git repository found on a military website. 778610: A stack buffer overflow vulnerability was found in Squid when acting as a reverse proxy. The vulnerability allowed for remote code execution and data leakage. The bug was fixed in Squid 4.10 released on 20 Jan 2020.
789034: A buffer overflow vulnerability was discovered in the ext_lm_group_acl helper of Squid versions 2.x to 2.7.STABLE9, 3.x to 3.5.28, and 4.x to 4.9. 790634: A vulnerability existed in GitLab where it accepted pushed branches that were 40-character hexadecimals, which could be named the same as a git hash. 794407: The CircleCI configuration for the `nextcloud/nextcloud-snap` project was vulnerable to leaking secrets when both the settings for allowing builds from forked pull requests and passing secrets to builds from forked pull requests were enabled. 796414: An authenticated read-only user was able to execute arbitrary shell commands on EdgeSwitch firmware v1.9.0, allowing them to escalate privileges. The vulnerability was fixed in EdgeMax EdgeSwitch firmware v1.9.1.
796487: A stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in the dy-server2 module, which allows an attacker to execute malicious code on a victim's browser when they view a vulnerable page. 797988: SNMP community string pages on EdgeSwitch 1G and 10G switches firmware v1.9.0 allowed read-only users to execute unauthorized tasks, resulting in community string disclosure. The vulnerability was fixed in EdgeMax EdgeSwitch firmware v1.9.1.
799881: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on an endpoint used for currency conversion. 800324: A buffer overflow vulnerability existed in several protocol parsers in tcpdump before version 4.9.2. 842035: An open redirect vulnerability was discovered in the www.shopify.dev environment, allowing an attacker to redirect a victim user to an unknown or untrusted website. 853284: The blog website was vulnerable to disclosure of internal information using hidden NTLM authentication.
