854726: A vulnerability was found in the unlock_time field in Monero transactions, which allowed an attacker to poll the local time of other nodes and potentially launch an eclipse attack. The vulnerability was caused by the validation rules for unlock_time values above 500000000, which were based on the local time of the machine running the Monero node rather than the network time. A patch was proposed to use the median timestamp over the past 60 blocks to verify the unlock_time.
856554: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered on the job page of GitLab. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to perform any action within the application that a user can perform, steal sensitive user data, and steal user credentials. The vulnerability was caused by the lack of input validation in the Kubernetes namespace field.
858598: A local privilege escalation vulnerability was discovered in Acronis Active Protection's anti_ransomware_service.exe. An unprivileged user can write/overwrite arbitrary files in arbitrary folders by controlling a privileged write with a hardlink in the quarantine folder. This can be used to escalate privileges to SYSTEM, as the anti_ransomware_service.exe runs with SYSTEM privileges. The vulnerability can be triggered by forcing the anti_ransomware_service.exe to copy a file to the quarantine folder through its REST API.
858603: A vulnerability existed in Acronis Active Protection where an unprivileged user could create a hardlink from a log file to the anti_ransomware_service.exe, causing the service to crash on every reboot due to a SHARING VIOLATION. This could result in the anti-ransomware protection failing silently, leaving the user vulnerable to ransomware attacks.
858608: The anti_ransomware_service.exe in Acronis True Image 2020 exposed a REST API that did not require authentication, allowing unprivileged users to add an arbitrary malicious executable to the whitelist or exclude the entire drive from being monitored by anti_ransomware_service.exe. This could have resulted in the disabling of the anti-ransomware service.
858674: A command injection vulnerability was discovered in the `wireguard-wrapper` module, which allowed an attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the victim's PC. The vulnerability was caused by insecure command concatenation, where a user input parameter was used inside a command that was executed without any check. The issue was reported to the maintainer and an issue was opened in the related repository.
859136: The Nextcloud Android client version 3.11.1 was vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack caused by a malformed intent. Malicious apps could crash the client by sending a deeplink `nc://login` that was not handled correctly by the `parseLoginDataUrl` method, causing the app to crash.
859395: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on http://www.grouplogic.com/files/glidownload/verify.asp, which could allow an attacker to execute malicious code on the victim's browser.
859962: A race condition vulnerability existed in Kubernetes versions 1.18.0 and below, allowing an attacker to bypass the apiserver proxy filter. By setting the hostname to a custom DNS server that returns different values with zero TTL, an attacker could access cloud metadata endpoints or localhost services through the apiserver proxy. The vulnerability was mitigated with a patch.
861744: A remote code execution vulnerability was discovered in Kibana 7.7.0, which allowed an attacker with write access to certain indexes to execute arbitrary code. The vulnerability was due to a prototype pollution in the "SIEM signal" feature. The vulnerability was reported to the vendor.
862835: A vulnerability was discovered in GraphQL that allowed for the execution of an introspection query through an unauthenticated WebSocket connection. This allowed an attacker to obtain the full GraphQL API with all methods and data types, potentially leading to more complex attacks.
864091: An RXSS vulnerability was found in the website, allowing an attacker to inject malicious code into the website's view parameter. This could lead to the attacker viewing or modifying information that the user is able to view or modify, as well as initiating interactions with other application users. The vulnerability could be used for various malicious purposes, including ad-jacking, session hijacking, bypassing CSRF protection, and crypto mining. The vulnerability could have been prevented by filtering input on arrival, encoding data on output, using appropriate response headers, and implementing a Content Security Policy.
865354: An arbitrary file upload and stored XSS vulnerability was discovered in the support request feature of a website, allowing a malicious user to upload any type of file and execute malicious code on behalf of the customer support representative. Whitelisting allowed file types for upload was suggested as a mitigation action.
865436: The administrator panel of the website mtngbissau.com was vulnerable to SQL injection, allowing unauthorized access to data. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted POST request to the login page.
865875: XMLRPC was vulnerable to brute-force attacks due to the presence of the admin username in the installer logs. Additionally, the pingback ping could be used to cause a denial-of-service attack on the server. The vulnerability also allowed for file disclosure, potentially exposing critical internal information.
867052: A vulnerability existed in the access control mechanism of Deck app, which allowed an attacker to inject tasks into other users' decks. This was possible due to a missing authorization check when moving a task to another deck, allowing an attacker to change the destination stackId parameter to that of a stack not belonging to them. As a result, an attacker could pollute the deck of other users.
867164: Passwords of all users were saved to the database table "oc_credentials" by the External storage app, even when the "Log-in credentials, save in database" option was not used. This allowed a local system admin with access to the database and Nextcloud config file to decrypt any user password, posing a security risk.
869450: An attacker could open a support incident for any user via a specific page, allowing them to trick the victim into taking actions such as clicking a link or opening a file that has been attached to the incident. The attacker could also view various PII about the user and monitor the victim's response. The vulnerability could be mitigated by locking down the feature to administrative access only.
870615: A vulnerability in Kaspersky Internet Security 2020 allowed an attacker to turn off the antivirus protection by injecting a DLL using the SetWindowsHookEx function. This could be exploited to bypass the antivirus protection and run malware undetected.
871156: A prototype pollution vulnerability was discovered in version 1.0.1 of the `plain-object-merge` module. The `merge` function allowed an attacker to inject properties on Object.prototype, potentially leading to Denial of Service (DoS), Remote Code Execution, or Property Injection attacks.
872304: An RXSS vulnerability was found in a website, allowing an attacker to view and modify user information, initiate interactions with other users, and potentially carry out malicious attacks. The vulnerability could also be used for ad-jacking, session hijacking, bypassing CSRF protection, and crypto mining. A fix was recommended, including filtering input on arrival, encoding data on output, using appropriate response headers, and implementing a Content Security Policy.
874482: A subdomain takeover vulnerability was identified in which the unclaimed subdomain "qa.myomnipod.com" was pointing to Acquia Cloud, allowing an attacker to claim the subdomain and potentially hijack the domain. The vulnerability was discovered through enumeration.
875049: The website allowed users to register with non-accepted email types, which could potentially be exploited by attackers.
876192: A misconfiguration in a content provider allowed a malicious app with storage permission to access all cookies in Brave for Android, potentially accessing private information from the user. The vulnerability was caused by the usage of `root-path` with path `.` in the File Content Provider, allowing access to all files in the Android system. The issue was resolved by implementing path checks to ensure that no internal file is used in the URI.
876719: A signedness issue in the ClassInfo message handler of the CS:GO client allowed for an array index underflow, leading to remote code execution. This vulnerability was present in any Source Engine game that uses Protobuf network messages. An attacker could execute arbitrary code on the computer of anyone who attempted to connect to the server, and gain control over the victim's computer. The vulnerability was exploited in two phases: bypassing ASLR and executing code.
882220: The website was vulnerable to a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attack through a crafted `X-Forwarded-Host` header. Attackers could pass malicious JavaScript to users, potentially accessing sensitive information and rewriting the HTML page. The suggested mitigation was to ignore invalid browser headers and filter metacharacters from user input.
882258: Confidential data in Nextcloud Deck app can be accessed by a new user with the same username after the previous user's account has been deleted. This vulnerability allows an attacker to view private information without any effort to restore data.
883693: Sensitive information, including Active Directory credentials, was leaked on a Department of Defense (DoD) asset due to the public display of a PHPInfo page. The vulnerability was reported and handled by DoD representatives.
883731: An Insecure Direct Object Reference vulnerability was found that allowed Minor accounts to modify their privacy permissions to restricted settings, including "Everyone". The vulnerability was fixed to ensure the protection of younger users on the platform.
888261: A vulnerability existed in Nextcloud versions prior to 18 that allowed an attacker to access a password-protected mail share without entering the password. This was possible if the password was provided when the share was created using the OCS endpoint. The vulnerability was fixed in Nextcloud 18.
891846: A memory corruption vulnerability (Out-of-Bounds) was found in the Linux Kernel up to version 5.5.6, specifically in the `set_fdc` function of the `floppy.c` file. The vulnerability could have allowed a local attacker to cause a denial of service or expose sensitive information. The issue was disclosed in February 2020 and assigned CVE-2020-9383.
892667: A subdomain takeover vulnerability was discovered in ██████ due to a dangling CNAME record pointing to an unclaimed ███████ webservice. An attacker could register the subdomain on ███ and gain full control over the contents served on the subdomain. The vulnerability was reported and the subdomain was claimed to prevent malicious use.
893922: IP-in-IP protocol allowed for arbitrary traffic to be routed by default, potentially leading to reflective DDoS, information leak, and bypass of network access controls. The vulnerability affected a large number of machines on the internet.
894518: Arbitrary JavaScript code could be executed on the Shopify Polaris demo page using the `postMessage` function, allowing an attacker to run code in a victim's browser.
899954: A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability existed in the message attachment fields of Rocket.Chat versions up to 3.3.3. Attackers could exploit this vulnerability to steal cookies, leak messages, delete messages, escalate privileges, and execute remote code.
900619: A reflected XSS vulnerability was discovered on transact.playstation.com that allowed an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript on the site. The vulnerability was due to insufficient validation of messages received from postMessage, which allowed an attacker to bypass checks and execute malicious code. The vulnerability could be exploited to steal cookies, tokens, and localStorage data.
901728: A vulnerability was found in a Social Club feature that allowed users to import their friends list from social media sites. An attacker could exploit this feature by tricking a victim into visiting a malicious site containing a specific script, which would link the victim's Social Club account to the attacker's Facebook account via CSRF. This would give the attacker control over the victim's Social Club account. The issue has been resolved.
903424: The Nextcloud desktop client did not validate the SSL certificate for nextcloud.com when users clicked "Register with a provider", allowing an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack and serve untrusted content in the trusted context of the client. This could lead to the theft of a user's email address and potentially other associated user information.
903872: A remote code execution vulnerability was discovered in OwnCloud's "files_antivirus" plugin, which allowed an authenticated administrator user to upload and execute arbitrary PHP code. The vulnerability was exploitable by setting the clamscan av path with the PHP interpreter path and uploading a file with PHP code. The impact of the vulnerability depended on the environment.
904064: A vulnerability allowed an attacker to inject HTML code into emails sent from a shared dashboard on a platform. The attacker could craft a believable spearphishing email coming from an email address owned by the platform. The vulnerability was due to the message not being fully sanitized for HTML characters before sending to the recipient.
904659: The website allowed access to PII of all site users via faulty access control to a specific endpoint. An attacker could access PII of all users by browsing to the endpoint. The suggested mitigation action is to restrict access to the endpoint to only administrative users.
904671: Sensitive information gathering was possible through the ability to view and modify requests and approvals via a specific endpoint. An attacker could identify hardware/software specifications of NIPRNET/SIPRNET assets and gather intel based on justification requirements in the requests. The suggested mitigation was to restrict access to this endpoint.
905543: A vulnerability in Shopify's API allowed low privileged users to add or remove cash from the sales register, despite not having access to the Shopify POS and having very low permission levels. The vulnerability was due to missing server-side permission checks on a vulnerable request, which allowed low privileged users to exploit it and supply another staff member's ID to show that they added or removed the cash. The vulnerability was exploitable by replaying the vulnerable request using a low privileged user session.
905641: An open S3 bucket was discovered where all uploaded files were public, resulting in information disclosure. An attacker could access and download any file uploaded to the bucket without authentication.
905679: PII (Full name/address/e-mail/phone) of all website users was exposed via a specific endpoint on the website, allowing an attacker to view the data. Access to this endpoint should have been restricted to administrative roles.
905688: A vulnerability was discovered in ServiceNow's e-mail notification modules that allowed an attacker to access PII of all users. By accessing the notification menu and selecting `Preview Notification`, the attacker could view a user's profile data, including their full name, rank, organization, e-mail address, physical address, and phone number. Mitigation actions include restricting access to the affected modules.
906322: The Github wikis of certain projects were editable by any logged-in user, posing a security and reputation risk for the company. This allowed a malicious actor to craft a message or note that could lead a user to download a malicious component.
906790: An account takeover vulnerability was discovered in File Sync & Share that allowed an attacker to change the email address associated with an account to any unverified email without requiring verification. This allowed the attacker to impersonate the victim and potentially steal important files. The vulnerability was due to a flaw in the name change functionality that also allowed changing the email address.
908162: A vulnerability was discovered in Acronis True Image that allowed an admin user to replace any of the executables in the LaunchDaemons folder, resulting in trivial privilege escalation to root. This was due to insecure folder permissions.
909863: A vulnerability existed in the Shopify Ping application that allowed low privileged users to create high privileged user's KITCRM authorization token and view their communication with the kit. This was possible by using the low privileged user's Shopify ping access token to create the high privileged user's KITCRM authorization token. The vulnerability was exploited by supplying the high privileged user's staff member id in the vulnerable request. The impact of the vulnerability was that low privileged users could give new instructions to the kit using the high privileged user's authorization token, making it difficult to track the attacker.
911880: License activation on account.mackeeper.com had no rate limit, allowing attackers to brute force the activation code and create any number of keys. The first request generated for the activation code did not validate G-Captcha verification, making it vulnerable to brute force attacks.
921288: Arbitrary file deletion was possible in Concrete5 version 8.5.4 due to a PHAR deserialization vulnerability. Attackers could send an arbitrary input value in the is_dir() function, which caused the PHAR deserialization bug, allowing them to delete arbitrary files. The vulnerability was patched by sanitizing user input.
921675: A vulnerability in GlassWire 2.2.210.0 allowed an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the targeted system by hijacking DLL files loaded from the PATH environment variable without verification. This could lead to privilege escalation to SYSTEM if the machine had at least one writable PATH directory. The GlassWire service loaded nine different DLLs as SYSTEM, while the GUI loaded one DLL as the currently logged-in user. Successful exploitation of the GlassWire service allowed an attacker to gain SYSTEM privileges and inject into the GlassWire service process at boot, while successful exploitation of the GlassWire GUI allowed a user to gain persistence.
921780: An improper authentication vulnerability was discovered on Snapchat's One Tap Password (OTP) login/logout flow. An attacker could log in to any account for which they had the user_id, which was exposed in several places and should not have been trusted in the request by the logout endpoint. This vulnerability allowed an attacker to log in as any user.
923020: A SQL injection vulnerability was discovered on the admin panel of Acronis hosting's development web service. The vulnerability allowed the attacker to gain access to the server and view three databases, including tables containing sensitive information such as user data and password resets. The vulnerability was reported to the Acronis security team.
923864: A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found on the website, allowing an attacker to inject malicious scripts into the website and potentially view or modify user information. The vulnerability could also be used for Ad-Jacking, Session Hijacking, Bypassing CSRF protection, and Crypto Mining. The recommended fix is to filter input on arrival, encode data on output, use appropriate response headers, and implement Content Security Policy.
924407: An outdated version of Cisco ASA VPN server hosted on us-az-vpn.acronis.com was found to have a Local File Disclosure/Delete vulnerability. An unauthenticated remote attacker could read and delete any file stored on the VPN server without authentication, including the VPN "lua" source code files. The vulnerability could break the VPN and prevent users from authenticating via the web portal.
924855: A SQL injection vulnerability was discovered in futexpert.mtngbissau.com, which allowed an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL queries and potentially access sensitive information.
925007: A blind SQL injection vulnerability was discovered on selfcare.mtn.com.af, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL queries and potentially gain unauthorized access to sensitive information.
925425: A vulnerability (CVE-2018-6389) in WordPress allowed unauthenticated attackers to cause a denial of service (resource consumption) by using a large list of registered .js files to construct a series of requests to load every file many times. The vulnerability was present in the script-loader.php file and could be exploited by sending a GET request to the load-scripts.php file with a large list of scripts to load. A fix for the vulnerability was provided by adding a rewrite rule to the .htaccess file.
925519: The XMLRPC.php file on the website play.mtn.co.za was enabled and could have been used for a potential application-level DoS attack via pingbacks, trackbacks, etc. The vulnerability was reported to the website's owner.
925585: A vulnerability was identified where certain development projects defaulted to the public NPM registry, instead of using the intended internal packages. This allowed for the creation of packages on the public registry that could have been registered with malicious intent and included in internal development. The issue was mitigated by PayPal with no evidence of prior malicious activity.
928255: A vulnerability in Gitlab allowed an attacker to delete user accounts without user interaction by sending a spoofed email to gdpr-request@gitlab.com, as the platform did not verify the request with a valid ID before triggering the Right to Access/Deletion, breaching GDPR law. The fix suggested was to add a second verification step, such as asking for DOB or government ID.
928280: A formula injection vulnerability was discovered in the CSV export feature of the Forms app in Nextcloud. When a formula is sent as an answer for a question that uses one of the two Response answer types which support text input, the formula gets reflected in the .csv export file without any type of sanitation. This vulnerability could allow a malicious actor to exfiltrate other participants' answers from the same sheet, read local files, or execute code.
931197: A vulnerability was discovered in the `socket.io` module version 2.3.0 that allowed an attacker to bypass origin protection using special symbols, including "`" and "$". This could be exploited as a typical CSRF vulnerability, allowing an attacker to send and receive WebSocket messages on behalf of a user. The vulnerability was discovered on Linux arch 5.7.9-arch1-1, using Node v14.5.0 and NPM 6.14.6, and was found to affect Mozilla Firefox 79.0b8.
941178: An SSRF vulnerability was discovered in the kube-apiserver cloudprovider scene, which allowed an attacker to create an admissionwebhook and cause an SSRF in the cloudprovider server. This vulnerability affected cloudproviders such as GKE, AKS, and EKS. By exploiting this vulnerability, an attacker could redirect the URL to the metadata server and potentially leak sensitive information.
942103: A vulnerability was found in the server code for testing ujs in Rails that allowed for server-side template injection, leading to remote code execution. An attacker could send a GET request with attack code to the test server, allowing them to execute arbitrary code on the server. The impact of this vulnerability was limited to devices running a test server for ujs, and did not have a significant impact on users.
943231: Memory corruption could be triggered by sending fragmented IPv6 packets to the loopback interface due to poor use of `IP6_EXTHDR_CHECK` macro. This could lead to a double free and potentially allow for privilege escalation. SOCK_RAW sockets reachable from the Webkit process on the PS4 could be exploited to trigger this vulnerability.
944025: A vulnerability was discovered in popular macOS apps with file-sharing functionality that did not delegate file quarantine to the OS, leading to a file quarantine bypass for downloaded files. Additionally, two insecure features in macOS were discovered that allowed for the execution of arbitrary local files by the full path at shortcut file opening. This behavior led to the discovery of two bugs in Chrome and Firefox. Multiple apps were affected, but some decided not to track the issue as a vulnerability.
945122: Arbitrary file creation was possible via a symlink attack on the syncagentsrv (Acronis Sync Agent Service). This allowed an attacker to create a file in an arbitrary location within the file system, including protected directories, and potentially elevate privileges up to Local System. The vulnerability was caused by the service blindly following symlinks without verifying the destination.
946384: The billing page on console.rockset.com was hidden from the menu for members, but a member-member privilege allowed access to the page through a direct URL, potentially exposing sensitive billing information.
946409: The Python library "yelp-cgeom" was installed on a Yelp-owned build server directly from the public PyPI registry instead of the internal Yelp registry due to a misconfiguration. The author of the library detected this and uploaded their own code under the same name, which was executed on the vulnerable machine, sending a callback with the machine's details.
946578: Multiple vulnerabilities were found in the MTN Afghanistan website that allowed unauthenticated attackers to cause a denial of service (resource consumption) by using a large list of registered .js files to construct a series of requests to load every file many times. The vulnerability was registered as CVE-2018-6389.
952166: The subdomain jet.acronis.com of acronis.com was pointing to an unclaimed Webflow service, making it vulnerable to subdomain takeover. The CNAME was pointing to proxy-ssl.webflow.com, and the subdomain was unclaimed/expired, allowing anyone to register it. An attacker could have hosted malicious content on the website or redirected visitors to another malicious website to spread malware/virus. The vulnerability was mitigated by claiming the custom domain in the Webflow portal.
953719: The subdomain www.jet.acronis.com of acronis.com was pointing to an unclaimed Webflow service, making it vulnerable to subdomain takeover. An attacker could have hosted malicious content on the website or redirected visitors to another malicious website to spread malware/virus. The vulnerability was mitigated by claiming the custom domain in Webflow portal.
956449: A vulnerability was discovered on the "link.avito.ru" subdomain of "www.avito.ru" that allowed an attacker to bypass restrictions for dangerous external links via trusted domain google.com. By using the google redirect functionality, an attacker could redirect a user from "link.avito.ru" to a malicious website through google.com.
959679: A vulnerability in the web services interface of Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software allowed an unauthenticated, remote attacker to conduct directory traversal attacks and read sensitive files on a targeted system. The vulnerability was due to a lack of proper input validation of URLs in HTTP requests processed by an affected device. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request containing directory traversal character sequences to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to view arbitrary files within the web services file system on the targeted device.
960082: A vulnerability was discovered in the web services interface of Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software that allowed an unauthenticated, remote attacker to conduct directory traversal attacks and read sensitive files on a targeted system. The vulnerability was due to a lack of proper input validation of URLs in HTTP requests processed by an affected device. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request containing directory traversal character sequences to an affected device, allowing them to view arbitrary files within the web services file system on the targeted device.
961046: A stored XSS vulnerability was discovered in the backup scanning plan name field of the Acronis cloud console. An attacker could store malicious JavaScript code in the plan name, which would execute when the plan is edited or viewed, potentially allowing for session hijacking or phishing attacks. The vulnerability was tested on Mozilla Firefox and Windows 10 and Kali Linux operating systems.
962604: A vulnerability in GitLab allowed Guest Role users to access Merge Request data that they were not authorized to view or edit via API. This vulnerability allowed revoked users to view the title, description, participants, commits, changes, pipelines, TODOs, diff versions, and approvals status of Merge Requests they created.
962889: A SQL injection vulnerability was discovered in the agent-manager of Acronis, which allowed an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL commands and potentially gain unauthorized access to sensitive data.
962902: A vulnerability existed in Rocket Chat versions 3.5.2 and 3.5.3 that allowed attackers to hijack user sessions by tricking them into performing a Self-XSS on the drag and drop functionality in the chat. This could allow attackers to read chats, change some information, and lock accounts by activating Two-Factor Authentication. The vulnerability could be mitigated by sanitizing the drag and drop functionality of the chat text box.
962908: A vulnerability in the web services interface of Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software allowed an unauthenticated, remote attacker to conduct directory traversal attacks and read sensitive files on a targeted system. The vulnerability was due to a lack of proper input validation of URLs in HTTP requests processed by an affected device. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request containing directory traversal character sequences to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to view arbitrary files within the web services file system on the targeted device.
964582: A buffer over-read vulnerability existed in the MPTCP parser of tcpdump versions prior to 4.9.2. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted packets to the network segment where the target system is running a tcpdump process that is decoding a live packet capture. The vulnerability could allow an attacker to inject executable code into the running program and take control of the process. The vulnerability has been patched in version 4.9.2.
964583: Versions of tcpdump before 4.9.2 were vulnerable to a buffer over-read in print-icmp6.c, which could be exploited by an attacker to inject executable code into the running program and take control of the process. The vulnerability was patched in version 4.9.2.
966494: A vulnerability in Acronis True Image 2021 allowed local privilege escalation via XPC service communication. The privilege helper tool only validated the code signature of the client, but not the version, allowing an attacker to use the old version of the app, which is vulnerable to injection. Injecting code into the old version allowed communication with the 2021 version XPC service, which allowed for local privilege escalation.
968355: A prototype pollution vulnerability was discovered in version 19.7.0 of the i18next internationalization framework. The vulnerability allowed an attacker to modify the prototype of a base object, potentially resulting in DoS, XSS, RCE, or other attacks. The vulnerability was caused by a lack of blacklisting of the `constructor` property in the `deepExtend` utility function used by the `addResourceBundle` function. The vulnerability required both `deep` and `overwrite` arguments to be set to `true` and for attacker-controlled input to be passed into the `resources` argument.
970157: A security vulnerability was discovered in Twitter that allowed hackers to bypass the old password screen and update a victim's password by using unrestricted rate limiting or password brute-forcing. This could lead to a complete takeover of the victim's account. The vulnerability was resolved by implementing rate limitation.
970878: Arbitrary HTML constructions could be injected on the page /admin/su/ due to insufficient escaping of special characters for the Error parameter, allowing an attacker to execute a cross-site scripting attack and potentially obtain user authentication information. The vulnerability has been fixed.
972220: Arpping module version 2.0.0 allowed for remote code execution via command injection when using the `ping` and `arp` commands. An attacker could execute arbitrary commands on the victim's PC by injecting malicious code. The vulnerability was patched by checking input before command execution.
972355: Private email addresses of GitLab users were leaked through a GraphQL query that allowed anyone to access them by providing the victim's username. This vulnerability could have been exploited for mass leakage of private emails.
973245: Arbitrary code execution was possible in version 4.2.0 of the `imagickal` module due to code injection while processing a photo, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the victim's PC. The vulnerability was patched by checking input before command execution.
973386: A command injection vulnerability was discovered in version 1.1.0 of the `curling` module for Node.js. The vulnerability allowed an attacker to bypass security checks for special characters and execute arbitrary commands, leading to remote code execution. The issue was caused by a regular expression that did not perform proper validation. The vulnerability was reported to the maintainer and a patch was recommended.
976137: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability was discovered on a subdomain of a website, allowing an attacker to execute malicious JavaScript code on a victim's browser. The vulnerability was caused by unsanitized user input on a GET request parameter.
976603: A vulnerability was discovered that allowed for a denial of service attack on any organization's SSO integration and the potential for account takeovers. The vulnerability was due to the ability to create an `entityId` identical to that of another organization except with a space at the end, which would prioritize the new `entityId` and allow for unauthorized access. The vulnerability was fixed before SSO became available to Grammarly customers.
977697: A stored XSS vulnerability existed in the merge requests pages of GitLab, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary actions on behalf of the victim, notably via GitLab API. The vulnerability occurred automatically without any need for victim interaction, despite GitLab CSP. The source branch was not sanitized when used as a title attribute in the _sidebar.html.haml file.
978823: An SSRF vulnerability allowed an attacker to read files from an AWS instance by sending a specially crafted request to the target server. The vulnerability was not properly fixed and could still be exploited.
979204: A DOM-based XSS vulnerability was found on the login page of https://partners.acronis.com/. An attacker could execute JavaScript code on users who open a specially crafted link, potentially leading to the theft of login credentials. The vulnerability was caused by HTML encoding that could be bypassed using JavaScript's unicode escaping.
980876: Kaspersky Internet Security for macOS was vulnerable to an AV bypass due to improper client authorization on the XPC service. A normal user could achieve full control of the extension and potentially disable all AV functionality. The vulnerability was caused by the system extension performing all of the AV functionality, like process monitoring, network monitoring, etc., and the configuration of the SEXT being performed via XPC. The service only verified if the Team ID was the one expected, but nothing else, allowing someone to talk to the XPC service who could inject code into a custom Kaspersky process.
981824: An email spoofing vulnerability was discovered in the DNS setup of hey.com, which allowed an attacker to send emails on behalf of other customers. The vulnerability was caused by the recycling of email addresses after 30 days, which allowed an attacker to register the same email address and use it to send emails from their own account. The vulnerability was reported to hey.com, and several recommendations were made to prevent similar issues in the future.
982130: The concrete5 CMS fetches an update JSON scheme over HTTP, which can be tampered with to point to a server controlled by an attacker. This, combined with the ability to set an arbitrary proxy for outgoing communications, can lead to remote code execution. An attacker with administrator privileges can exploit this vulnerability.
982293: A security vulnerability allowed hackers to bypass the old password screen on Twitter and update a victim's password by using unrestricted rate limiting or brute forcing. This could lead to a complete takeover of the victim's account.
983077: A stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in the advanced vetting settings page of a program due to unsanitized input being passed into a Markdown component. This allowed a program member to inject malicious code into the example Custom Digital Agreement (DCA) generated based on the program name, which could be exploited when the program was in sandbox mode. The impact was limited to Program Managers who were authorized to update the program name, and programs in sandbox mode did not contain real vulnerability data.
983710: A SQL injection vulnerability was discovered in ImpressCMS during the database configuration process. An attacker could inject malicious code into the "Database name" field, which would create a new database and execute arbitrary code on the database. The vulnerability was caused by the failure to escape backticks in the code.
984654: A reflected cross-site scripting (RXSS) vulnerability was found in the URI path of a website. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to view or modify user information and initiate malicious attacks. The vulnerability was fixed by filtering input on arrival, encoding data on output, using appropriate response headers, and implementing a content security policy.
985133: A weak password was used to secure a PDF containing sensitive information, which was cracked using a common word list. The plaintext password was then used to gain access to an unprotected configuration file, potentially allowing an attacker to join a secure communication channel.
986365: A reflected XSS vulnerability was discovered on /www/delivery/afr.php, which allowed an attacker to bypass a previous fix by closing the script tag and opening a new one. This vulnerability could have allowed an attacker to perform arbitrary actions on behalf of the victim.
990048: Improper validation at the partners login allowed an attacker to get the OTP of the victim on both the attacker's number and the victim's number. The vulnerability was due to the lack of strict checks on the `country_isd` parameter. The backend generated the OTP for the `phone_number` parameter but appended the `country_isd` parameter to the `phone_number` parameter before sending the SMS without any major checks.
992618: An improper access control vulnerability was found on a sub-domain of a website, allowing anyone to view and delete tickets that were not meant to be accessible to everyone. The vulnerability could potentially lead to unauthorized access and deletion of sensitive information.
993722: Unrestricted access to the quiesce function via a PUT request to dss.api.playstation.com REST API made the application unreachable for an uncertain amount of time. An attacker could disrupt the availability of the application in a sustained manner through multiple PUT requests for quiescence.
995347: The vulnerability allowed an attacker to use the "url" parameter to trick users into downloading malicious files or scripts from external resources. This could potentially compromise the accounts, computers, and identities of users. The issue was caused by a lack of validation on the "url" parameter.
996041: A vulnerability was discovered in Reddit that allowed for unrestricted file uploads. An attacker could upload a corrupted image file that would cause web cache poisoning and a complete denial of service. The issue affected all users who followed the account that posted the corrupted image, and there was no way to get rid of it. The vulnerability was tested in Firefox, Safari, and Opera, but not in Google Chrome.
996122: The Adobe Connect platform had insufficient session expiration and lacked password protection, allowing an attacker to brute force meeting rooms and access chat history and uploaded files containing personal identifiable information. This vulnerability put military staff at risk.
996273: A Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability was found in the login page of a website, which allowed an attacker to perform malicious actions on behalf of the server. By using the fetch() API property of JavaScript, the attacker was able to send a cross-domain request and perform SSRF. This exposed the victim's IP address to an external server controlled by the attacker, allowing them to determine the victim's physical location through IP tracing. The vulnerability could also be used to launch port scans and exploits on visitors to the website.
996535: A post-based reflected cross-site scripting (RXSS) vulnerability was discovered on a certain domain via the frm_email parameter, due to unsanitized input. An attacker could execute JavaScript code on the victim's behalf by crafting a CSRF PoC.
996540: A vulnerability was discovered in Apple Pay in-app or on-site payments, where the same payment cryptogram could be used multiple times within 24 hours for different stores, allowing attackers to commit fraud. The attack was possible due to the lack of checks during Apple Pay payments and the fact that RBK Money did not check the price shown on the Apple Pay payment sheet, only the price sent on the request. Stolen Apple Pay cryptograms could be used for much larger/arbitrary payments.
997350: A vulnerability was found in a Shopify application where the preview link was being leaked to third-party sites, allowing malicious users to preview all actions in the store without the need for a password. This could compromise the security of the store and its owner.
997376: An external service interaction vulnerability was found on a website, which allowed an attacker to induce the application to interact with an arbitrary external service, such as a web or mail server. This could be used to trigger interactions using other service types and could allow the vulnerable server to be used as an attack proxy, exposing highly vulnerable internal services that are not otherwise accessible to external attackers.
997381: An XML injection vulnerability was found on a website's parameter, which could potentially allow an attacker to gain unauthorized access to sensitive data. The vulnerability was reported to the website's owner for further action.
998398: Prototype Pollution vulnerability in Swiftype's deparam function allowed an attacker to inject malicious code into the website, leading to XSS attacks.
998925: A vulnerability in Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software allowed an unauthenticated, remote attacker to conduct directory traversal attacks and read sensitive files on a targeted system. The vulnerability was due to a lack of proper input validation of URLs in HTTP requests processed by an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to view arbitrary files within the web services file system on the targeted device.
998935: A Post-Based reflected XSS vulnerability was discovered on a certain domain due to unsanitized input inside a specific parameter, allowing an attacker to execute JS code on the victim's behalf. A CSRF PoC can trigger the vulnerability.
1002188: A potential HTTP Request Smuggling vulnerability existed in nodejs, allowing an attacker to use two same header fields to make a TE-TE HTTP Request Smuggling attack. This could lead to the smuggling of the request and disruption of the user experience.
1004412: Possible LDAP username and password were disclosed on Github, which could have allowed insider threats to use the credentials for lateral movement and privilege escalation.
1004964: Personal support requests made to a certain website were being disclosed to the public through a publicly accessible endpoint, posing a critical privacy issue.
1009046: A vulnerability was reported where premium templates could be used in a free plan on a website. Upon notification, the issue was addressed.
1010340: A vulnerability (CVE-2020-27194) in the Linux kernel's eBPF verifier was discovered that allowed an unprivileged attacker to create BPF socket filter programs that could read and write Out of Bounds, leading to arbitrary kernel read-write access and a highly reliable Local Privilege Escalation (LPE) exploit. The vulnerability affected the kernel 5.8.* stable branch and could have impacted many distributions. The issue was patched with commit 5b9fbeb75b6a98955f628e205ac26689bcb1383e.
1010787: A vulnerability was found in the Uber Device Returns Management Platform registration page, which allowed unauthorized access to personally identifiable information (PII). The authentication was not integrated with Uber's central authentication, and a similar domain name could be registered to bypass the email domain restriction. Flat access control allowed access to site content and control of the entire platform.
1010858: A cache poisoning vulnerability was discovered on www.acronis.com, which could potentially distribute various attacks by exploiting vulnerabilities such as XSS, JavaScript injection, and open redirection. The vulnerability was caused by different requests hitting the same cache due to the presence of URL parameters and certain request headers.
1011888: Improper sanitization on the company field of the registration form on Informatica's website allowed for a blind XSS attack. An attacker could inject a payload that would execute when an admin accessed the user record, potentially leading to the theft of sensitive information and the installation of malware.
1012249: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found in the search form of a website, allowing an attacker to execute malicious scripts in the victim's browser by tricking them into clicking a specially crafted link. The vulnerability was found in the POST keyword parameter and could potentially lead to the theft of user cookies or modification of webpage content. A proof of concept was provided.
1015406: A SQL Injection vulnerability was discovered in a web application, where the POST rnum parameter was not properly sanitized, allowing an attacker to interfere with the database queries and obtain sensitive information. The vulnerability could lead to the dumping of personal data or authentication bypasses.
1017189: A blind stored XSS vulnerability was found on the pac.whs.mil website. An attacker could inject malicious code into the description field of a request, which would execute when an administrator views the request. This could potentially lead to the leakage of administrator credentials. The suggested mitigation is to sanitize the input being inserted into the description field.
1019389: A vulnerability was found in the HEY macOS app that allowed an attacker to execute code on the victim's computer by uploading an executable file without setting the `com.apple.quarantine` attribute in the metadata of the file. This allowed the file to be executed on macOS without being checked by Gatekeeper. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a malicious file as an attachment in a message, which would execute without any warning or alert.
1019425: A stored XSS vulnerability was found in the header image upload function at https://manage.booth.pm/design/edit. The server failed to properly validate the provided `Content-Type` upon file upload, allowing an attacker to upload a HTML file with arbitrary JavaScript embedded, resulting in a stored XSS on BOOTH's sandboxed domain s2.booth.pm.
1020371: Files can be uploaded by unauthenticated users even after their account has been closed on the Hey email service. This vulnerability allows attackers to upload files to the service without authorization, potentially leading to data breaches or other security issues.
1020472: Sensitive SQL data call information was revealed due to a system error in the login page of a military website. An attacker could use this information to gain knowledge of the SQL system and launch future attacks. The suggested mitigation is to remove any mention of the SQL database calls in the stack trace error.
1021776: The `/create-payment` API endpoint on cs.money allowed an attacker to generate cancelled transactions in a user's transaction history by using only their Steam ID. The attacker could access the transaction and cancel it, leading to confusion for the user and potentially resulting in the account being banned.
1023572: Sensitive information belonging to other users of the Salesforce instance at acronis.secure.force.com was leaked due to loose permissions on the Event object for unauthenticated Guest users. An attacker could craft a HTTP request directly to the Aura API using built-in controller methods to extract this information. The vulnerability was remediated by enforcing record level security on the vulnerable object.
1023787: A stored XSS vulnerability was found in Nextcloud Talk's markdown editor. Attackers could create a link element with a javascript URL and execute arbitrary JavaScript code on the victim's browser when they click the malicious link. The vulnerability affected Internet Explorer, even though CSP blocked the JavaScript from running.
1023899: A regular expression denial of service vulnerability was discovered in ActiveRecord's PostgreSQL Money type. The vulnerability had an execution time with a quadratic growth proportional to the length of the string, causing denial of service. The vulnerability was caused by the regular expressions used to convert strings to integers. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by inputting long strings in a request body, leading to 100% CPU usage and denial of service.
1026146: Due to a lack of access control, an anonymous attacker could compromise the administrator account on the Questionmark Perception system, allowing them to view all fields of the questions, results, and personal information of the participants. The vulnerability was exploited by using publicly accessible service descriptions and bypassing access controls. The suggested mitigation actions include removing the service description and reconfiguring the system to deny all requests without the SOAP "Trust" header.
1027873: The NGINX configuration of Shopify allowed for potentially hitting internal NGINX locations on *.myshopify.com by making use of the `X-Accel-Redirect` header via a configured App Proxy. An attacker could have exploited this vulnerability to access sensitive information. However, no actual impact was determined. The vulnerability was mitigated by setting the `proxy_ignore_headers X-Accel-Redirect` directive in the NGINX configuration.
1028396: A reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), and XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability was found in a 3rd party vendor used by HackerOne. The vulnerability was remediated after HackerOne worked with the vendor.
1031321: A broken link in a page on developer.twitter.com allowed anyone to create a GitHub account with a username that could be used to impersonate another user. This could lead to malicious content being posted on the impersonated user's GitHub account, potentially damaging their reputation.
1031644: A DOM XSS vulnerability was found on http://talks.lystit.com due to an insecure postMessage handler being registered, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript on another user. The vulnerability was fixed after being reported.
1034257: A misconfiguration in an interstitial page allowed links to be indexed by third parties, potentially exposing vulnerable endpoints and unlisted videos/photos. The issue affected a specific set of customers and was caused by browser plugins and email software. The problem was addressed by instructing crawlers not to index the interstitial page.
1035742: An authentication bypass vulnerability was discovered in the administrator panel of a website, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive information. The vulnerability was exploited by navigating to a specific endpoint, which authenticated the user as an administrator without proper credentials. A suggested mitigation action is to issue a 403 response when attempting to access the vulnerable endpoint.
1036877: A blind stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was discovered due to an insecure contact form on a military website. The form did not properly sanitize user input, allowing for the insertion and submission of dangerous characters. An attacker could submit a blind XSS payload through the form, triggering XSS in the admin panel and revealing critical information such as the administrator's IP address, backend application service, titles of mail chimp customer and internal subscription emails, and admin session cookies.
1039750: A stored XSS vulnerability was discovered in the Intense Debate comment system, allowing users to inject malicious code into comments and potentially attack admins or other users on the blog. The vulnerability was triggered by allowing images in comments and could result in stealing cookies and secret tokens or editing HTML/CSS/JS content for phishing attacks.
1039805: Multiple URLs were found to be vulnerable to Clickjacking during security testing. The vulnerability was due to the server not returning an X-Frame-Options header, which could allow an attacker to embed the website's content into another site and potentially hijack keystrokes. The impact of this vulnerability could be significant, as it could lead users to unknowingly enter sensitive information into an attacker-controlled frame.
1039821: A vulnerability existed in HackerOne's Salesforce lead submission process that allowed for second-order SOQL injection through the email and campaign name parameters. This allowed an attacker to inject arbitrary SOQL commands, potentially leading to unauthorized access to sensitive data. The vulnerability was due to string interpolation in the SOQL query and has since been fixed.
1040166: A vulnerability existed in curl versions prior to 7.71.0, where the FTP protocol implementation did not skip the IP address verification step for incoming PASV responses. This allowed an attacker to perform port scanning on behalf of the server where curl is running, leading to potential information disclosure and further attacks.
1040373: A password authentication bypass vulnerability was discovered in the account linking feature, allowing an attacker to link accounts without providing the correct password confirmation.
1040471: Recently discovered vulnerabilities allowed bypassing rate limiting protections on a login page, enabling brute force password guessing attacks.
1040533: A XSS Reflected POST-Based vulnerability was found in `https://www.intensedebate.com/ajax.php`. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to perform a phishing attack or a CORS attack. The vulnerability was triggered by injecting malicious code into the `txt` parameter of the POST request.
1040639: An XSS Reflected POST-Based vulnerability was found on `https://www.intensedebate.com/update/tumblr2/{$id}`. The `$_POST['txtCode']` parameter was not sanitized, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary code. The vulnerability required the attacker to create a site and invite the victim with full permissions to trigger the XSS. The impact of the vulnerability was that an attacker could perform a phishing or CORS attack.
1041173: A vulnerability was found in Happy Tools that allowed users to change their email without verification. An attacker could exploit this by changing the email of a user to a non-existent email and then attempting to invite that user to the organization, causing a permanent denial of service.
1042716: Clear text authorization headers were stored in the `.async-search` index, which contained the results of async searches. This allowed super users to access the credentials of other users, potentially leading to lateral movement or impersonation. The vulnerability was present in Elasticsearch versions up to and including 7.10.0.
1043360: The Node.js http2 server was vulnerable to denial of service attacks due to a resource exhaustion issue caused by an 'unknownProtocol'. Attackers could establish an arbitrary number of connections to the server, causing the process to leak file descriptors and consume excessive memory, leading to a system crash. The vulnerability affected any code that relied on the http2 server, and the attack had low complexity, making it easy to trigger a DOS on an unprotected server.
1043372: A client-side Denial of Service vulnerability was reported, causing a Denial of Service by loading up the memory usage. The vulnerability occurred when visiting a corrupted bounty table of a target program, resulting in the browser tab crashing and displaying an "Out Of Memory" error message.
1043385: A misconfiguration of a Private NPM registry allowed a nodejs-based project to install a malicious module generated by an attacker instead of a normal module. This occurred when an attacker registered a higher version with the same name as a private module with the Global Registry, causing the project to download and install the malicious module from the Global Registry. This could have resulted in arbitrary code execution on the affected hosts.
1043480: A vulnerability was discovered in GitLab that allowed a remote hacker to download files of any branch in a public project where all permissions were set to member-only. The hacker could exploit a bug in GitLab's link to download files, which allowed anyone on the internet to download the file through the link for a few moments after an admin or someone with the permission to download the files of the branch clicked on the link. This could lead to a data leak.
1043804: A reflected DOM-based XSS vulnerability was discovered in the "posttitle" parameter of https://www.intensedebate.com/js/getCommentLink.php. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to steal cookies of logged-in users, redirect users to other websites, or perform actions on behalf of the user.
1044285: It was possible to download the latest digital purchased order attachment for stores that have the Digital download app installed, by setting the checkout_token to be empty. When the checkout_token was nil, all orders were returned and the latest order from the list was selected. The issue was resolved by validating the checkout_token before fetching an order.
1044716: A SQL injection vulnerability was discovered in the www.hyperpure.com website. An attacker could use a PUT request to create a sales lead with a random sales ID in the database by exploiting the vulnerability. The vulnerability was proven by executing AND and OR statements.
1044869: A vulnerability was discovered in Shopify that allowed staff with no permissions to list and accept billing promotions. This was due to improper access control in the GraphQL API endpoints related to billing promotions.
1045844: A stack overflow vulnerability was discovered in cURL's FTP wildcard functionality (CVE-2020-8285). The vulnerability could be triggered by adding/crafting files in the server, potentially leading to a denial-of-service attack.
1046630: A vulnerability was discovered on www.streamlabs.com that allowed an attacker to take over a victim's account by adding a null byte character in the state parameter of a CSRF PoC. The attacker could then host the CSRF PoC on their website and trick the victim into visiting it, which would connect the attacker's Twitch account to the victim's Streamlabs account. This would allow the attacker to log in to the victim's Streamlabs account using their Twitch account and take it over.
1047086: A heap buffer overflow vulnerability was discovered in ImageMagick version 7.0.10-45 while processing a malformed TIFF file, which could result in a crash of the software. The vulnerability was caused by a read of size 1 at an address located 0 bytes to the right of a 248-byte region, which was allocated by the thread.
1047119: A vulnerability was found in the ability to create plug-ins without rate limiting. The vulnerability has been fixed.
1047124: A vulnerability was discovered in the email subscription feature of Stripo.email that allowed an attacker to bypass the rate limit and send bulk emails to the victim. The attacker could add a fixed throttle in Burp Suite to avoid the 429 response and send multiple emails to the victim. No rate limit was implemented in the email subscription feature, making it vulnerable to abuse.
1047447: The HostAuthorization middleware in Ruby on Rails did not properly sanitize the Host / X-Forwarded-For header, allowing for redirection to a hostile site. This vulnerability could be exploited by an attacker to redirect a user to a malicious site.
1048322: A vulnerability in FreeBSD 12 allowed SMAP to be bypassed by userland, which downgraded the security properties of the OS and was a building block for exploitation chains. The bug was in the fault handling of the `copyin()` and `copyout()` functions, which did not clear `%RFLAGS.AC` after a fault occurred, effectively disabling SMAP until the kernel returned to userland. This allowed userland to open large windows where the kernel executed with SMAP disabled, making exploitation of common vulnerabilities easy/trivial.
1048540: The UID parameter on a user operations API endpoint in a system used by a military branch did not validate the caller's permission to view information on the UID entered, enabling unauthorized personnel and student data extraction. An unauthenticated, unauthorized external attacker could obtain the full names, emails, military branches, and scores of all users registered in the system.
1048571: An open set of endpoints on a system enabled scraping of sensitive data without authentication or authorization. The endpoints included the ability to view data and perform injections against the database service. Additionally, a stored XSS attack was possible on an inserted profile. The suggested mitigation was to remove or guard unused endpoints with authorization checks.
1049375: An unauthenticated attacker could bypass SAML authentication on a Rocket.Chat instance by exploiting an unauthenticated Meteor method called `addSamlProvider`. This method allowed disabling SAML signature verification, which could enable an attacker to log in as an arbitrary user with administrative privileges. The vulnerability affected all versions of Rocket.Chat that supported SAML authentication using a provider named `Default`.
1050193: An open redirect vulnerability was found on the website intensedebate.com, where the parameter "goto" in the URL was reflected in the HTTP header response "Location". This could allow an attacker to redirect users to malicious websites for phishing and other attacks.
1050196: Approximately 1000 personal records, including phone numbers and email addresses, were leaked through a PDF uploaded on a website on October 7th. The affected individuals were in contact with the DoD.
1050244: Two-factor authentication enforcement in Nextcloud was bypassed, allowing attackers to gain access to user dashboards. An attacker with administrator access could create a new user and add them to a group with two-factor authentication enforcement. The attacker could then log in as the new user and bypass the two-factor authentication enforcement by replacing the oc_sessionPassphrase token with the first oc_sessionPassphrase session.
1050454: An information disclosure vulnerability was found in outdated versions of Atlassian Jira Server and Data Center, allowing remote and unauthenticated attackers to view custom field names and custom SLA names via the /secure/QueryComponent!Default.jspa endpoint. The vulnerability was fixed in version 8.5.8 and 8.11.1.
1050733: An XSS vulnerability was discovered on a subdomain of WordPress.com. An attacker could exploit the vulnerability by inserting malicious code into the "Redirect address" field of the Poll block's Confirmation Message, which would execute when an authenticated user submitted a poll and potentially steal their cookies.
1050912: A vulnerability existed in the PHP info page, which allowed an attacker to obtain detailed information on the system and PHP configuration, including the exact PHP version, OS version, loaded PHP extensions, and their configurations. This information could be used to research known vulnerabilities and aid in the exploitation of other vulnerabilities.
1051029: Sensitive information, including an authentication API key, was leaked in a publicly accessible JavaScript file on the bb3jobboard.topechelon.com website, potentially leading to information disclosure.
1051192: An insecure use of the `yaml.load()` function in the Kubernetes `test-infra` tool allowed for code injection via a malicious YAML file, resulting in command execution. The vulnerability was present in the `Gubernator` configuration update process. The issue was resolved by replacing the vulnerable function with its secure equivalent, `safe_load()`.
1051369: A blind stored XSS vulnerability was triggered on the backend of a website, allowing an attacker to capture administrator actions, extract database credentials, access private information, and steal cookies. Mitigation actions include sanitizing input on the backend.
1051734: A vulnerability was found in the report functionality of IntenseDebate, which allowed an attacker to delete any comment on a site where the report functionality was enabled. The issue was caused by the lack of rate limiting on the report functionality, which allowed an attacker to spam the report button and delete the comment after a certain number of reports.
1051885: An application used by a government agency had an old endpoint that accepted insecure credentials, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive information and the ability to modify, insert, and delete data. The vulnerability was caused by the use of weak login credentials and could have been mitigated by disabling them and restricting external access to the portal.
1054282: The "user_ldap" plugin in Owncloud allowed for protocol smuggling over the LDAP password field, which could be exploited by an attacker with admin privileges to communicate with internal services over plain text protocols like SMTP and Redis. The vulnerability was caused by the lack of input validation for newline characters in the password field. An attacker could use this to send arbitrary emails and even achieve remote code execution. The severity of the vulnerability was low due to the preconditions required for exploitation.
1054382: A vulnerability was discovered in Burp Suite that allowed an attacker to force unsolicited hidden requests, potentially leaking the auditor's real public IP address, Windows NetNTLM hashes, or causing a denial of service. The vulnerability was fixed in versions 2020.12 and 2021.2.
1054526: A Stored XSS vulnerability was found in the Custom Style section of wordpress.com. An attacker could execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the attacked website and user, potentially stealing session cookies or performing requests in the victim's name. The vulnerability was exploited by creating a malicious Style and inviting the victim to become a manager or administrator.
1055823: A Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability was found in the Add a custom Integration feature on console.helium.com. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to retrieve private meta-data from the AWS EC2 instance running on the server by creating a custom HTTP integration and setting the integration endpoint to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data. The endpoint input is not validated, making the application vulnerable to the SSRF.
1056611: A vulnerability in Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software allowed an unauthenticated attacker to conduct directory traversal attacks and obtain read and delete access to sensitive files on a targeted system. The vulnerability was due to a lack of proper input validation of the HTTP URL. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request containing directory traversal character sequences. The impact of the exploit could allow the attacker to view or delete arbitrary files on the system.
1057269: A PII information leak was discovered on a website, where a file containing personal emails and names of over 100 individuals was publicly accessible. The file was arranged neatly in rows and columns, making it easy for attackers to add the information to their database. The suggested mitigation actions were to take down the file and add an authentication mechanism to view it.
1057419: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on a website for invalid paths, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript code on the victim's browser. The vulnerability was mitigated by sanitizing the path input or switching to a generic error message.
1058015: A vulnerability was discovered that allowed for full account takeover on a military website. An attacker could intercept a victim's login request and use it to change the victim's password, gaining full control of their account.
1059395: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on a page that had a parameter vulnerable to improper input sanitization. Attackers could exploit this vulnerability to execute malicious Javascript or steal data. The vulnerability has been reported for remediation.
1060518: There was no rate limit in sending OTP codes, allowing an attacker to send an unlimited number of SMS messages and potentially bomb the victim's mobile inbox, causing MTN to lose charges for the SMS messages.
1060541: A vulnerability was found in the MTN Online website that allowed for brute force attacks on OTP codes due to the lack of rate limit protection on the submit endpoint. Attackers could send unlimited requests to guess the correct OTP code before it expires.
1061199: A Reflected XSS vulnerability was found on play.mtn.co.za, with the parameters injectable through the "?page=2" parameter. Malicious JavaScript could access cookies and local storage, potentially leading to session impersonation, and could modify the contents of the page, opening up possibilities for social engineering attacks.
1061204: A vulnerability (CVE 2020 14179) allowed a remote attacker to view custom SLA fields and use them to make a JQL query, resulting in sensitive information disclosure. The endpoint did not authenticate users, leading to broken authentication.
1061292: Sensitive personal information of contractors and employees registered on TAMS was exposed due to an unauthenticated API endpoint that allowed anyone to view registration details and attachments without proper authentication. The vulnerability has since been fixed.
1061591: A vulnerability existed in all versions of Nextcloud (18-20) that allowed users to act as a different user via DB-stored credentials. The issue was related to LDAP authentication and external SMB shares via DB stored credentials. The problem was that there was no check if the current user in the session was the same as the user for whom the credentials were stored. As a result, the stored credentials in the database were incorrect, and users could act as the admin user, accessing SMB shares on the network with higher privileges than themselves. The vulnerability was patched with a security conform bugfix.
1061664: Sensitive data of Khan Academy was leaked due to a signup bypass vulnerability that allowed unauthorized access to the alerta dashboard without email confirmation.
1062380: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on a search functionality of a website, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript code on the victim's browser. The vulnerability was caused by improper input sanitization. The impact of the vulnerability was considered medium.
1062803: Sensitive data related to DoD production, admin, localhost, and other directories were leaked due to a misconfigured AWS S3 bucket, allowing unauthenticated users to access and download the files without any restrictions. The suggested mitigation action is to properly configure the S3 bucket to prevent the listing of sensitive files.
1063039: A Phar deserialization vulnerability was found in Concrete5 versions 8.5.4 and 8.5.5 RC1. The vulnerability allowed malicious users to inject arbitrary PHP objects into the application scope, leading to the execution of arbitrary PHP code. Successful exploitation required an admin account.
1063256: Remote code execution was possible on a website due to an outdated Drupal version, specifically versions before 7.58, 8.x before 8.3.9, 8.4.x before 8.4.6, and 8.5.x before 8.5.1. This vulnerability was identified as CVE-2018-7600 and affected multiple subsystems with default or common module configurations. The vulnerability allowed remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.
1063298: The employee panel of a web application had unauthorized access due to default credentials being used. An attacker was able to bypass the login function and gain access to the admin panel by changing the value of a form. This vulnerability could have allowed the attacker to perform malicious actions within the platform.
1063371: Sensitive information was leaking through a Department of Defense (DoD) owned website, including personal mail IDs, names, phone numbers, client IP, and addresses. The information was contained in a clear, readable PDF document, which was a privacy violation and lacked sufficient protection mechanisms. The vulnerability required immediate remediation.
1063493: The website https://promosandbox.acronis.com was vulnerable to HTTP Request Smuggling, which could have been exploited by an attacker to redirect users to arbitrary resources. The vulnerability was assigned low severity since it was limited to the sandbox environment and did not affect other Acronis websites.
1063627: HTTP Request Smuggling was possible on https://consumer.acronis.com, allowing an attacker to redirect users to arbitrary resources. The vulnerability was assigned low severity since the domain was not in use and other Acronis websites did not load any resources from there.
1064095: A stored XSS vulnerability was discovered in the Acronis Cyber Protect Console, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the attacked website and user. The vulnerability was triggered by creating a protection plan with a payload in the name field, which was not properly sanitized.
1064149: The API endpoint for sending location data on the WHO app did not properly validate latitude and longitude values, allowing for the storage of non-existent coordinates in the database. This could have been exploited to affect the availability or integrity of analytics data and falsify user data.
1064869: An Insecure Direct Object Reference vulnerability was discovered on Shopify's Shop app, allowing an attacker to access checkout details, including shipping addresses, by iterating over checkout IDs. The vulnerability only affected checkouts created within the Shop app for shops belonging to Shopify employees. The issue has been fixed by implementing checks to ensure that only the owner of the checkouts can access them.
1065041: A Google API key was leaked to the public, exposing several endpoints vulnerable to the Geocode API. The vulnerability could potentially cost companies extra money and cause denial of service. The cost of the vulnerability was identified as $5 per 1000 requests.
1065128: A vulnerability was discovered on the website dashboard.myndr.net/auth, where an attacker could send a large number of requests without any rate limit mechanism to determine the victim switch serial and proceed with the registration process.
1065134: A publicly available Firebase Database in the Zego Sense Android app allowed attackers to access and modify sensitive data. 1065167: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on a website due to lack of input validation, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript on behalf of the victim. The vulnerability was remediated by sanitizing the input on the affected parameter.
1065186: The Dubsmash login endpoint had a weak rate limit mechanism that allowed attackers to perform brute force attacks and gain access to user accounts by bypassing the rate limit error message. 1065485: Multiple security vulnerabilities were found in the Grinch Network's website, which could have allowed an attacker to gain unauthorized access to sensitive data, execute arbitrary code, and launch attacks on users. 1065495: A security vulnerability was present in the hackyholiday challenge, where the flags for the first 10 submissions were publicly disclosed.
1065516: A security vulnerability was present in the hackyholidays CTF, where all the flags for the challenges were exposed in a message. This could potentially allow unauthorized access to the flags and compromise the integrity of the CTF.
1065517: A security vulnerability was discovered in the hacky holidays CTF website that allowed an attacker to obtain all the flags by running a simple script. The vulnerability was critical and could have had serious consequences.
1066083: The "My Account" page in ███████mil was vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CSRF) due to a failure to verify the CSRF token used when a user made changes to their account details. 1066410: An Open Redirect Vulnerability was discovered in Clario due to a Google API key leak and security misconfiguration. 1066851: A security vulnerability was present in the "12 Days of Hacky Holidays" game, which was a text-based RPG that required Ruby to run. 1067004: An information disclosure vulnerability was found in outdated versions of Atlassian Jira Server and Data Center, allowing remote and unauthenticated attackers to view custom field names and custom SLA names via the /secure/QueryComponent!Default.jspa endpoint. 1067276: A publicly accessible endpoint in a website did not validate its parameters, allowing an unauthorized attacker to send arbitrary emails from the website's controlled email servers.
